title: Legacy CRM Data Model — Managed Package Organization and Functional Domain Structure
summary: The complete data model architecture of a legacy life sciences CRM, organized across multiple managed packages with 200+ custom objects spanning account management, business planning, field execution, compliance, and content delivery functional domains.

findings.managed_package_organization: The data model is distributed across multiple managed packages, each with its own namespace prefix. The primary package contains core CRM objects (accounts, calls, samples, territories). Extension packages add domain-specific capabilities: one package for advanced engagement features, another for compliance and regulatory functions, another for content management, and additional packages for region-specific or industry-specific extensions (including connectors for expense management, provider data networks, organizational mapping, messaging platforms, and reference data services).
findings.account_management_domain: 40+ objects covering healthcare provider and organization management. Core objects handle account records, addresses, affiliations, and relationship hierarchies. The affiliation model supports bidirectional relationship mapping between providers and organizations with role-based classification. Address objects support multiple address types per account with territory assignment linkage.
findings.business_planning_domain: Five sub-domains: Account Plan (17+ objects for strategic account planning with objectives, tactics, and stakeholder mapping), Activity Plan (8+ objects for cyclical visit planning with target frequencies and product priorities), Calendar (scheduling and availability management), Call Plan (visit sequence optimization), and Plan Cycle (temporal planning periods that govern all business planning activities).
findings.execution_domain: Four sub-domains: Call (20+ objects covering visit recording, attendee tracking, product discussion capture, key message delivery, and post-visit workflows), Compliance (7 objects for regulatory tracking including sample distribution rules and HCP interaction limits), eDetailing/CLM (15+ objects for closed-loop marketing content delivery, slide-level analytics, and presentation session management), and Email (template-driven compliant email with tracking).
findings.admin_and_configuration_domain: Four sub-domains: User (profile, permission, and role hierarchy management), Territory (geographic and organizational territory definition with product alignment), TimeOfTerritory (representative-to-territory temporal assignments supporting territory realignment), and Product (9 objects covering product hierarchy, product groups, therapeutic area classification, and message/indication relationships).
findings.additional_functional_domains: Activity History (historical interaction aggregation), ADA Lite (next best customer and message recommendation engine), BestTime (visit timing optimization based on provider availability patterns), Clinical Trial (8 objects for trial site and investigator tracking), Data Change Request (7 objects for field-initiated data correction workflows with approval routing), HCO/HCP Dashboard (organization and provider summary visualization), Ratings (9 objects for provider profiling scores and segmentation), Search Before Create (duplicate detection for account creation), and Document Management (content versioning and compliance-tracked document distribution).
findings.version_evolution: The data model follows a versioned evolution pattern where new releases add objects and fields while maintaining backward compatibility with existing deployments. Version comparison documentation tracks which objects and fields were added, modified, or deprecated between major releases, enabling customers to assess upgrade impact on their customizations and integrations.
